O.outcome_detail: agreement in pupils' rankings and class-section placement

result.effect: median rank change 18 places; 51.6% placed in the wrong section; 31.8% displaced by at least half a section

cells.quote: The Otis Intelligence Test and the Illinois Examination were given by the same person in the junior high school grades of the Chicago Normal School during 1919 and 1920, and when 120 of the pupils were ranked on the basis of scores in the two tests—using only the intelligence division of the Illinois Examination—the median change of rank from one test to the other was found to be 18 places.
cells.note: The comparison is between two tests administered to the same pupils; the text does not define a better-performing test.

cells.quote: The coefficient of correlation between the two sets of scores, by the rank difference method, was 0.642.
cells.note: The positive correlation indicates association between the two test rankings, not a treatment advantage.

O.outcome_detail: agreement in students' rankings and two-class placement

result.effect: median rank change 6.7 places; 26% placed in the wrong class; 5.5% displaced by at least half a class

cells.quote: The Thurstone and the Brown University tests when similarly given to 54 students of college freshmen grade showed a median change in rank of 6.7 places, as compared with a maximum possible change of 27 and a random change of 18.
cells.note: The comparison is between two tests administered to the same freshmen; the text does not define a better-performing test.

O.outcome_detail: agreement in students' rankings and two-class placement

result.effect: median rank change 10.4 places; 32.8% placed in the wrong class; 6.3% displaced by at least half a class; correlation 0.613

cells.quote: A sophomore group of 64 students when given these two tests showed a median change in rank of 10.4 places, with 14 whose change of rank was less than 5 places, and 31 whose change of rank was less than 10 places, but with 5 whose change of rank was more than 30 places.

O.outcome_detail: Agreement in pupil rankings and four-section class placement

result.effect: rank correlation 0.642; median rank change 18 places; 51.6% placed in the wrong section; 31.8% displaced by at least half a section

cells.quote: The coefficient of correlation between the two sets of scores, by the rank difference method, was 0.642. If these 120 pupils had been divided on the basis of the intelligence scores of one test into four class-sections of ordinary size, 51.6 per cent of them would have been in the wrong section according to the other test, and 31.8 per cent of them would have been out of place by an amount equal at least to half the range of such a class-section.
cells.note: The positive association coexisted with substantial disagreement in individual rankings and placements.

O.outcome_detail: Agreement in freshman student rankings and two-class placement

result.effect: correlation 0.74; 26% placed in the wrong class; 5.5% displaced by at least half a class

cells.quote: The Thurstone and the Brown University tests when similarly given to 54 students of college freshmen grade showed a median change in rank of 6.7 places, as compared with a maximum possible change of 27 and a random change of 18. Twenty-four students changed rank less than 5 places, and 33 less than 10 places. Dividing these students into two classes in the order of their scores on one test would have placed 26 per cent of them in the wrong class according to the other test, and would have put 5.5 per cent of them out of place by as much as half the range of such a class. The correlation between scores is 0.74.
cells.note: The tests were positively associated but did not produce identical rankings or class assignments.

O.outcome_detail: Agreement in sophomore student rankings and two-class placement

result.effect: correlation 0.613; 32.8% placed in the wrong class; 6.3% displaced by at least half a class

cells.quote: A sophomore group of 64 students when given these two tests showed a median change in rank of 10.4 places, with 14 whose change of rank was less than 5 places, and 31 whose change of rank was less than 10 places, but with 5 whose change of rank was more than 30 places. The correlation between these scores is 0.613. Dividing the sophomore group into two classes on the basis of the scores in one test would have placed 32.8 per cent of them in the wrong class according to the other test, and would have put 6.3 per cent of them out of place by at least half the range of each class so formed.
cells.note: The tests were positively associated, with substantial disagreement in rankings and class assignments.

O.outcome_detail: Practical usefulness of guidance between foreign language and manual work

result.effect: two-year practical trial; no printed numerical effect size

cells.quote: For guiding the pupil in the choice between two studies—a foreign language and manual work—the Otis scores have proved by a two-year trial in the junior high school named above to be of real practical value. With a few adjustments in cases of extreme divergence from scholarship records, this classification has proved workable and in general satisfactory.
cells.note: The study reports practical experience rather than a randomized comparison.
